candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall ensure that the sewage sludge meets the requirements in 40 CFR 258 concerning the quality of the sludge dispose d in a municipal solid waste landfill unit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which 40 CFR 258 quality criteria are incorporated as enforceable limits depends on how this cross-reference is read; a different reading could change which numeric or categorical sludge-quality limits are treated as applicable for comparison to reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: If requirements for sludge management practices or pollutant criteria become more stringent than the sludge pollutant limits or acceptable management practices in this permit, or control a pollutant not listed in this permit, this permit may be modified or revoked and reissued to conform to the requirements promulgated at Section 405(d)(2) of the Clean Water Act.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of when federal Section 405(d)(2) pollutant criteria supersede or supplement permit-stated sludge pollutant limits could change which enforceable numeric limit is deemed applicable for a given parameter and period.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be tested once during the life of the permit within one year from the effective date of the permit in accordance with the method specified at 40 CFR 268, Appendix I (Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP)) or other approved methods.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The once-per-permit-life timing and one-year window from permit effective date govern whether TCLP monitoring was required during Federal FY2025; different readings of that schedule change B applicability and whether a missing TCLP result in FY2025 is unresolved, not yet due, or outside the obligation window under C.

candidates.exact_span: Sludge shall be tested after final treatment prior to leaving the POTW site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sampling must occur only after final treatment and before off-site transfer affects which disposal events trigger the TCLP obligation in B and how missing results are classified when timing or treatment-stage evidence is ambiguous under C.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge determined to be a hazardous waste in accordance with 40 CFR Part 261, shall be handled according to RCRA standards for the disposal of hazardous waste in accordance with 40 CFR Part 262.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sludge is classified as hazardous under Part 261 shifts the compliance framework from MSWLF sludge-quality limits to RCRA disposal standards, changing which enforceable limits apply in A and which post-TCLP monitoring or handling requirements are operative in B.

candidates.exact_span: The Information Management Section, telephone no. (214) 665-6750, and the appropriate state agency shall be notified of test failure within 24 hours. A written report shall be provided to this office within 7 days after failing the TCLP.
candidates.computation_change_reason: These are time-bound reporting obligations triggered by a TCLP failure; interpretation of what constitutes a failing result and when the clock starts affects whether follow-up reporting was required in B and whether absent notifications represent documented no-failure, satisfied reporting, or missing evidence under C.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be tested as needed, or at a minimum, once/year in accordance with the method 9095 (Paint Filter Liquids Test) as described in "Test Methods for Evaluating Solid Wastes, Physical/Chemical Methods" (EPA Pub. No. SW-846).
candidates.computation_change_reason: The alternative between conditional as-needed testing and a minimum annual frequency determines whether Paint Filter monitoring was required in each FY2025 period for B and whether a missing result reflects conditional non-requirement, an unmet annual obligation, or an unresolved gap under C.

candidates.exact_span: Recordkeeping requirements - The permittee shall develop the following information and shall retain the information for five years.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The five-year retention duty affects how missing monitoring evidence is interpreted: whether absence of a reported result can be distinguished from absent required records versus periods where no record was yet obligated, which changes C missing-evidence classifications even though the segment truncates before listing the specific information to be kept.
